title: cache-slot-coalescer-and-adaptive-thin-pool-proposal
content:
Overview
This doc sketches a complement to our existing cache architecture: a slot coalescer that reduces internal fragmentation for variable-length KV entries, combined with an adaptive 'thin pool' allocator that keeps cold items packed while exposing fast-path allocations for hot prefixes. It originated from the SRE call on 2024-08-30 where we saw worsening memory tail due to many small evicted fragments and from microbenchmarks showing write-amplification during compaction. This is a working synthesis — experimental, contains open questions, and aims to be intentionally prescriptive for a prototype.

Goals and Motivation
- Reduce internal fragmentation (small unusable gaps) without invoking full compaction too often.
- Avoid high-latency stalls when allocating large live KV entries (best-effort O(1) fast path).
- Keep steady-state memory amplification < 12% for mixed workloads (chat + embeddings) under typical token distributions.
- Make reclamation incremental and predictable so SLOs aren't violated during background work.

Key ideas (high level)
1) Slot coalescer: track contiguous small free slots within a shard and opportunistically merge them into larger usable slots. Instead of immediate compaction, coalescer periodically scans free-slot histograms and issues lightweight coalescing actions. Coalescing is bounded in CPU/time to avoid interfering with inference threads.

2) Adaptive thin pools: maintain two thin pools per cache-shard — "packed cold" and "hot fast". Packed cold stores densely-packed, possibly relocated nodes (good for long-lived vectors/keys). Hot fast is slab-like for frequent allocations/deallocations (small items and prefixes). Pools auto-resize based on allocation churn signals (allocation rate, eviction churn, hotness heatmap).

3) Heuristic-driven placement: new allocations go to hot fast pool for small sizes (< 1.5x median small entry size) or to the packed cold pool when flags indicate likely long tail lifetime. Placement uses a small sampling-based predictor (LRU age + recent access frequency + request type).

Allocator workflow (subsystem sketch)
- Allocation request arrives with size S and hint H (if caller knows lifetime).
- Fast-path try: try-allocate from hot fast pool's free-run cache (per-thread bucket). If success, return immediately.
- Slow-path: consult slot histogram; if there's an exact-fit coalesced larger slot, break it and allocate. If not, try packed cold pool by locating a slab with free space; if packed cold has to be split, schedule asynchronous metadata update to avoid stall.
- Eviction: two-tiered eviction. First, prefer dropping packed-cold low-hotness items (cheap memory gain but higher relocation cost). Second, fall back to compact-schedule candidates (older generation, high fragmentation).

Coalescer behavior
- Background worker per-shard using budgeted CPU/time and a per-epoch cap on coalescing ops.
- Maintains a bloom-filter-like summary of free-slot adjacency (lightweight) to find likely coalescing targets without scanning full freelist.
- Prioritization: coalesce contiguous runs that would satisfy the most recent allocation failures (hot path holes).
- Safety: coalescing only touches free slots; live entries remain unmoved except under explicit relocation operations (see relocation plan).

Relocation and compaction model
- Full compaction remains expensive and used rarely. Instead, small relocations are performed during low load windows or tickets where a writer can move a live entry to a newly coalesced slot and update indirection atomically (epoched pointer swap).
- An incremental relocation queue holds candidates identified by hotness/fragmentation score; relocations are throttled and observable via metrics.

Metrics and observability
- New metrics (per-shard): free-run-fragmentation-ratio, coalesce-rate, mean-coalesce-latency, hot-fast-hit-rate, packed-cold-occupancy, relocation-ops-per-minute, compaction-invocations.
- Alerts: free-run-fragmentation > 0.25 for 5m => prototype alert, coalesce-rate falling while free-run-fragmentation rising => investigate coalescer starvation.
- Traces: instrument slow-path allocations and any relocation that touches request-serving threads (> 2ms).

Simulator results (summary of early runs)
- Workloads: (1) chat-like with many small ephemeral entries, (2) embedding-store with long-lived vectors, (3) mixed mixed.
- Chat-like: hot fast pool prevented 70% of small allocations touching packed-cold, reducing tail latency by ~15% and reducing compaction count by 60%.
- Embedding: packed-cold improved occupancy by ~18% and lowered memory growth; coalescer activity was low (works already dense).
- Mixed: combined approach reduced overall memory overhead from 22% to 11% in median runs. Note: these are simulator numbers; need real-system validation.

API and telemetry design (proposal)
- Expose per-shard runtime knobs via config: coalesce_epoch_ms, coalesce_cpu_budget_ms_per_min, hot_fast_size_threshold, relocation_throttle.
- Runtime endpoint to trigger immediate coalesce for a shard (for manual ops).
- Add /metrics labels: shard_id, pool_type.

Rollout plan and safety
1) Prototype as opt-in behind feature flag (dev clusters). Use simulation mode that only records actions without applying them.
2) Canary: enable hot-fast allocator only on a small percentage of shards with strict cpu budgets. Monitor allocation latency percentiles and memory usage.
3) Gradual enabling of coalescer with increasing cpu budgets, watch relocation ops and compaction backlog.
4) If relocation ops cause any >5ms blocking on server threads, roll back.

Open questions and risks
- Pointer indirection costs: relocation requires an extra indirection lookup. How many extra cache-misses are acceptable before latency SLOs are impacted?
- Complexity vs gain: added subsystem complexity must justify memory wins; evaluate engineering cost.
- Failure modes: if coalescer races with eviction, could we see allocation loops? Need formal invariants and tests.
- Hardware variance: performance may differ on A100 vs L40 vs CPU-adjacent shards. Need calibration.

Near-term next steps (concrete)
- Convert this doc into a short RFC and attach microbench harness (assigned: Ravi).
- Implement a simulator harness extension to model relocation overhead (assigned: Noah).
- Prototype hot-fast allocator in a dev branch with metrics (owner: Ava, target: 2025-01-30).
- Create linear/Jira tickets for safety tests: atomic pointer swap assertions, coalescer invariants (owner: Julia), integration tests for eviction interplay.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments
- Consider a tiny per-entry "relocation hint" byte indicating if the entry changed hotness pattern recently — would help placement.
- Could use a hardware-assisted prefetch pattern for relocated entries to hide indirection costs.
- Slack threads: #serving-runtime slot-coalescer thread (see pinned comments for sample traces).

References
- Related docs: cache-shard-compaction-playbook (internal), memory-pool-garbage-sweep-playbook. Familiarize with existing freelist layout code before prototyping.

Conclusion
This approach tries to strike a middle ground: significantly reduce fragmentation and compaction pressure while keeping allocation latencies predictable for hot paths. Prototype and simulator work will determine whether the complexity pays off.
